entries.speaker: D
entries.text: 1.30 hrs forward time. We arrived last night at 10.00 local time.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We are staying at the ‘Malasia Hotel’, there is a super swimming pool. At 1.30pm we went on a tour to see some temples. We saw 3, one had a huge reclining Buddha (Thailand is 95% Buddhist), nearly all the buddhas were gold plated. When Mum & H went back, Dad, F & I looked at some shops, we bought a big canteen set for 12 people, with serving utensils.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We woke up very early, for our tour of the water market. Mum didn’t come. We left the river and went down a canal, house barges and houses on stilts lined the water way. At one temple, we saw someone extracting a cobra’s poison. At somewhere else, we met a baby elephant. We had a really interesting time.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Yesterday, instead of flying to Singapore, Dad found out that the plane was delayed in Frankfurt, every time we rang up, they said, oh just a few more hours. F, H & I were in the pool, when Mum came and said that Shaun and Keena were in their house at Bangkok. We got out and then went to meet Keena. Liam and Rory were with her, she took us to see the Palace, the Temple of the ‘Emerald Buddha’. There were some really beautiful paintings and scenes along the wall of religious stories and legends. We had a Thai meal at their house - cow pat (noodles!), crab, soup. After dinner I played with Rory. From Keena’s house, we went to the airport, we were to board the plane at 4am.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We arrived 10am Singapore time. We rang up Tan and he send someone to pick us up. Qantas was paying for a Hotel and lunch and dinner for us. After a wash and rest, Tan came and took us to a Restaurant. We met his wife there, and filled up with delicious Chinese food. Then Tan took us shopping. I wanted a nice parasol, but we could only find plastic umbrellas. Then we went to look for a radio / cassette for Mum and Dad. They bought one and we bought two records (101 Dalmatians and Peter, Paul and Mary album). Dad, Tan and I went just across the road from the Hotel, to get a little Philips pocket radio, with earphones. It suddenly began to rain violently, so we made a dash to the Hotel. We didn’t get too wet, the rain was very warm.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: On the flight Singapore / Australia, we stopped for about ¾ of an hour in Jakarta. We didn’t get out, we were too tired. We had dinner and breakfast on the plane, the food wasn’t very good.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At last, very very tired, we arrived in Sydney. We collected our luggage and took a bus to the Inter-Australian airport. There, we took an hour flight to Brisbane. From the air, we could see the whole of Sydney, and the Opera House. When we got near Brisbane, it seemed to stretch out everywhere. Little, red-roofed houses, all with their own bit of garden. When we arrived, we couldn’t find Grandma or Grandad. At last, we drove to Daphne’s house. Grandma and Grandad picked us up from there. Daphne gave me some antiseptic cream for my Impetigo sores.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Brisbane is very nice and clean, apart from the stations, which have all been scribbled on, lots of the men have long hair in pigtails. Lots of people wear shorts. Everything is very expensive. Everything is nice and green and lush. We had a lovely paw-paw. At night, I saw a big toad. On TV there is Sesame Street, Dad’s Army and Liver Birds.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We’ve got a lovely house, in The Gap. It has a swimming pool, and a big garden. My bedroom is downstairs, near the pool. It’s got a private bathroom, with a basin and shower, all in blue. There is a lovely big kitchen, with a hatch to dining room, and a lovely big lounge. We will have to do a lot of work to the garden.
